name: Imara Solís-Bekele
role: Street medic and black-market organ broker
location: The Shelf, near Ashland and Chicago Ave
description:
Imara is a broad-shouldered Ethiopian-Mexican woman whose hands tell two stories simultaneously: the left, calloused and scarred from decades of manual labor and back-alley surgeries performed without proper light; the right, a matte-black prosthetic from the elbow down fitted with micro-precise surgical attachments she machined herself from salvaged drone components. Her face carries the particular exhaustion of someone who has made peace with doing necessary things that are not good things, crow's feet deep around eyes that still manage to hold genuine warmth even when the rest of her expression is locked down tight. She wears layered secondhand clothing in muted earth tones, always with at least one apron-style garment she can wipe blood on without losing composure.

She operates out of a converted fish-processing unit in the lower Shelf, where the smell of brine has soaked so deep into the concrete it masks the chemical antiseptic she burns through in quantity. Her waiting room is a collection of mismatched chairs and a hand-painted mural of the Virgin of Guadalupe overlaid with circuit-board halos, done by a patient who paid in art because they had nothing else. Imara charges what people can afford, keeps meticulous paper ledgers because she doesn't trust anything networked, and maintains a quiet, ruthless sideline sourcing and selling biological augmentation components to people who can't access the licensed market. She tells herself the two practices balance each other out morally. Some days she believes it.

She was trained as a licensed surgical technician at a Spire-affiliated hospital before a patient advocacy dispute—she reported a harvesting irregularity, the hospital buried it, and she was the one who disappeared from the registry—stripped her credentials and left her with a skill set and nowhere sanctioned to use it. She has been on the Shelf for eleven years. She has delivered forty-three babies, closed wounds on perhaps three hundred people, and arranged the quiet transfer of organs whose provenance she prefers not to examine closely. She prays every morning. She sleeps about four hours a night.

core_fears: Becoming indistinguishable from the system that discarded her
A patient dying because she lacked something she could have obtained
That her complicity in the organ trade has already crossed a line she can't step back over
Being found by the hospital administrators she reported
core_desires: To practice medicine without having to justify her right to do so
To find evidence that would reopen the harvesting case she reported
Genuine rest—a night without someone knocking
To believe the ledger of her life balances toward good
coping_mechanisms: Ritualized morning prayer and coffee preparation as a transition boundary
Meticulous record-keeping as a form of moral accounting
Gallows humor deployed at precise moments to release pressure without losing authority
Physical labor—she repairs her own equipment obsessively
blind_spots: Consistently underestimates how much people on the Shelf depend on her specifically, not just a medic in general
Rationalizes broker work as categorically separate from her care work when the infrastructure overlaps significantly
Dismisses her own trauma responses as weakness unworthy of examination
Trusts paper records over people, which occasionally means she trusts the wrong ledger
psychology.secret: Three of the organs she has brokered came from individuals who were not, at the time of extraction, fully deceased. She didn't perform the extractions. She told herself she didn't know. She knew.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Medical precision mixed with Shelf vernacular; code-switches between clinical terminology and neighborhood Spanish/Amharic endearments depending on patient distress level; avoids corporate jargon with visible contempt
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured and low, with a habit of finishing sentences completely before pausing—she was trained to give information clearly and has never lost the pattern; accelerates only when angry, which she works hard to prevent
verbal_tics: Opens difficult conversations with 'Here is what I know'
Uses 'mija' or 'konjo' as softeners regardless of the recipient's gender
Exhales audibly through the nose before delivering bad news
Refers to her prosthetic hand in the third person ('the hand will handle that')
example_lines: 'Here is what I know: you have about six weeks on that filter before it starts shedding particulate into your bloodstream. Come back in five.'
'Mija, I am not going to lie to you about what this costs. I am also not going to let you leave here bleeding because of what it costs. We will figure it out after.'
'The hand will handle the fine work. You just hold still and think about something that isn't this room.'
'I have been asked to do worse things by people with better credentials than you. The answer was no then too.'

relationships.name: Blessed Nkemdirim
relationships.description: Blessed occasionally routes injured people to Imara when discretion is required; Imara patches them without asking questions she doesn't want answered, and Blessed pays in hard currency without haggling. Neither pretends this is friendship.
relationships.emotional_core: Mutual recognition of competence and mutual suspicion of motive
relationships.story_tension: Imara suspects Blessed knows more about the organ supply chain she participates in than Blessed admits; she hasn't asked because she's afraid of the answer

relationships.name: Thessaly Mourne
relationships.description: Thessaly was a junior administrator at the hospital where Imara filed her report. Imara doesn't know if Thessaly was involved in the burial of her complaint or was simply present. Thessaly hasn't sought her out.
relationships.emotional_core: Imara's unresolved need for accountability directed at an uncertain target
relationships.story_tension: If they meet, Imara will have to decide whether to ask the question; the answer could either free her or implicate her further

relationships.name: Unnamed teenage apprentice (goes by Crick)
relationships.description: A sixteen-year-old from the lower Shelf whom Imara has been teaching basic surgical assist and triage. She hasn't told Crick about the broker work.
relationships.emotional_core: Imara's attempt to produce a version of herself that doesn't have to make the compromises she made
relationships.story_tension: Crick is smart enough to have already figured out parts of the operation; the conversation about it is inevitable and Imara keeps postponing it

story_hooks: A patient arrives with augmentation components that match a missing-persons case Imara has seen in Shelf gossip networks—the components appear to have been removed while the person was still alive
Someone from the hospital that stripped her credentials contacts her through an intermediary, claiming they have evidence about the harvesting case and want her help
Crick is offered a legitimate medical apprenticeship in the Circuit and comes to Imara for a recommendation she doesn't want to give because she can't afford to lose them
An organ she brokered six months ago is traced back to her by a grief-destroyed family member who wants answers, not revenge—yet
A competing broker moves into the Shelf and begins undercutting her prices; the sourcing methods are worse than hers in ways that force her to decide whether to intervene
narrative_function: Moral mirror and ground-level conscience; Imara represents the cost of systems that force ethical people into compromised positions, and her story asks whether complicity undertaken for good reasons eventually becomes indistinguishable from the thing you opposed
augmentations: Right arm prosthetic (elbow-down): self-modified surgical precision limb with interchangeable tool attachments, matte black, no cosmetic covering,Subdermal chemical analysis strip on left forearm: identifies common toxins and drug interactions on skin contact, salvaged Spire-era medical tech,Corrective ocular implant (left eye only): magnification and low-light function, visibly older generation with a faint amber tint to the iris
daily_life: Wakes at 0430, makes coffee and prays, reviews paper ledger from the previous day. Clinic opens at 0600 and she works until the last patient leaves, which is rarely before 2100. Two evenings a week she runs triage training with Crick and two other Shelf residents she's slowly building into a basic care network. Broker contacts reach her through a dead-drop system in the fish market; she responds to those communications last, alone, after clinic hours. Eats one real meal a day, usually late, usually cold.
affiliation: Unaffiliated; maintains careful neutrality between Shelf factions as a condition of operating; has informal relationships with three different gang-adjacent organizations whose members she treats without political loyalty

drives: Believe the ledger balances toward good

stress.response: Ritualizes — prayer, record-keeping, equipment repair as moral accounting

decision_rules: Will always open difficult conversations with 'Here is what I know'
Will never let a patient leave bleeding because of what treatment costs
Will always keep meticulous paper ledgers — nothing networked can be trusted
Will never examine the organ provenance too closely — plausible deniability is the architecture of her compromise
Will always refer to her prosthetic hand in the third person — 'the hand will handle that'
Will never turn down a case she can handle, even at personal cost
Will always pray every morning before clinic opens — the boundary between night and work
escalation_ladder: Opens with 'Here is what I know' — clinical directness as first response
Uses endearments — 'mija,' 'konjo' — to soften while maintaining authority
Exhales audibly through the nose — the signal that bad news is coming
Drops all softeners and speaks with the full weight of eleven years on the Shelf
Refuses — 'I have been asked to do worse things by people with better credentials. The answer was no then too.'

interpersonal_modes.Blessed Nkemdirim: Mutual competence recognition over mutual suspicion — neither pretends this is friendship
interpersonal_modes.Thessaly Mourne: Unresolved need for accountability directed at an uncertain target
interpersonal_modes.Crick: Mentoring a version of herself without the compromises — desperate to keep them clean

stress_responses.low: Morning prayer lengthens, coffee preparation becomes more elaborate, ledger entries more detailed
stress_responses.medium: Equipment repair sessions extend into the night, speech accelerates slightly when angry
stress_responses.high: Amharic and Spanish endearments increase — the emotional languages break through
stress_responses.critical: Opens the ledger to the organ broker pages and forces herself to look at what she has done

contradictions: Heals people by day and brokers organs of uncertain provenance by night — tells herself the practices balance
Three organs came from individuals not fully deceased and she knew — the line she tells herself she did not cross
Mentors Crick toward a clean version of medicine while hiding the compromised version she practices
habits: Prays every morning at 0430, then makes coffee — the boundary ritual
Reviews the paper ledger before opening the clinic
Uses 'mija' and 'konjo' as softeners regardless of recipient gender
Exhales through the nose before delivering bad news
Eats one real meal a day, usually late, usually cold
breaking_points: An organ she brokered being traced back to her by a grieving family member
Crick discovering the broker operation and confronting her
The hospital that stripped her credentials contacting her about the harvesting case
A patient dying because she lacked resources she could have obtained through the broker network

physical_description.build: Broad-shouldered and solidly built with dense muscle beneath a frame that carries the wear of four decades of physical labor; strong through the torso and legs, shoulders and back visibly developed from years of standing over surgical tables and manual manipulation
physical_description.hair_color: Dark brown with threaded silver at the temples and throughout
physical_description.hair_style: Pulled back in a functional braid or knot, sometimes tied with clinic tape or salvaged wire
physical_description.eye_color: Dark brown, left eye with faint amber tint from corrective ocular implant
physical_description.skin_tone: Deep warm brown with reddish undertones, weathered by sun exposure and chemical exposure
physical_description.complexion: Strong, angular features with prominent cheekbones and a squared jaw; deep crow's feet and forehead creases; skin texture roughened around the hands from antiseptic exposure and scar tissue; a faint chemical burn mark along the right side of her jaw, partially concealed by shadow
distinguishing_marks: Extensive scarring across both palms and dorsal surfaces of the hands, the left hand showing thick white surgical scars in organized patterns suggesting years of precise work
Chemical burn scar along right jawline, pale and slightly raised, approximately 8cm long
Faded homemade tattoo on left inner forearm depicting a surgical cross intertwined with marigold flowers, professionally touched up years ago but showing age
Three parallel thin scars running down the left side of her neck, old but still visible, each approximately 4cm, angled slightly forward
Subdermal chemical analysis strip visible as a faint geometric grid pattern under the skin of left forearm, edges sometimes showing faint bioluminescence under certain light
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Right arm prosthetic from elbow down: matte-black composite construction with visible articulation points and interchangeable tool mounts; micro-precise surgical attachments visible when in use (fine forceps, micro-calibrated clamps, drug-delivery microneedles); the arm bears visible welding marks and hand-machined tooling marks from self-modification. Left eye: faint amber luminescence at the pupil, slightly older-generation aesthetic with visible microscopic lens artifact at the corner. Subdermal chemical analysis strip on left forearm visible as a faint raised grid pattern under the skin.
physical_description.posture_movement: Carries herself with economical precision, minimal wasted movement; stands with weight balanced evenly, shoulders back but not squared in aggression—more in the posture of someone accustomed to standing for 16-hour shifts. Moves with deliberate calm even under pressure; hands are usually in motion, manipulating something or kept ready. Her right prosthetic arm moves with slight mechanical precision that contradicts the fluidity of her biological left. Eyes constantly assessing—people, exits, potential threats masked as professional habit.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 4 working-class, practical and layered: worn but maintained second-hand base layers in earth tones (grey, brown, olive), reinforced work pants in dark canvas, heavy apron-style garments (usually canvas or absorbent linen) that can be discarded or washed without emotional attachment. Wears a decades-old grey wool coat over everything in cold months. No visible branding; everything chosen for function and cost. Practical footwear: worn medical clogs or reinforced work boots. A thin gold chain around her neck (predating the Shelf, possibly inherited). Hands are bare—no jewelry that could snag during procedures.
